summary:
LUNAR COMMAND is an interactive lunar mission survival simulator designed to introduce students and space enthusiasts to the challenges of establishing and maintaining a human habitat on the Moon.

In this browser-based game, players take command of a four-person lunar crew and must keep them alive for 30 lunar days (sols). They must manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, electrical power, radiation shielding, and thermal comfort.

Players make strategic decisions every sol by selecting actions such as recycling resources, deploying solar panels, operating a greenhouse, improving radiation protection, conserving resources, and maintaining critical systems. Random mission events and resource consumption create realistic decision-making challenges.

The objective is to complete the 30-sol mission while keeping the crew safe and maintaining sufficient resources. LUNAR COMMAND transforms complex lunar habitat challenges into an accessible and engaging educational experience that encourages systems thinking, problem-solving, and engineering awareness.
details: LUNAR COMMAND – Mission Survival Simulator 1. Introduction LUNAR COMMAND is an interactive browser-based educational simulation that places the player in charge of a simulated lunar outpost. The mission is to ensure the survival of a four-member crew for 30 lunar days (sols) while managing limited resources and responding to unexpected environmental and operational challenges. 2. Problem Statement Establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon requires careful management of life-support systems, energy, food production, radiation protection, and thermal conditions. Understanding how these interconnected systems affect one another can be challenging for students. LUNAR COMMAND addresses this challenge through an interactive mission simulation. 3. Main Features - 30-sol lunar survival mission. - Four-member simulated lunar crew. - Oxygen, water, food, power, radiation shielding, and thermal resource monitoring. - Six strategic mission actions. - Resource recycling and conservation. - Solar power management. - Greenhouse and food production simulation. - Radiation protection and critical system maintenance. - Random mission events and environmental challenges. - Mission progress tracking and command log. - Final mission debrief and performance score. 4. How It Works At the beginning of the mission, the player receives a limited set of resources. Each sol, the player selects one action to support the crew and maintain the habitat. The simulation then applies resource consumption and possible mission events. The player must balance competing priorities and make decisions that allow the crew to survive until Sol 30. 5. Technology Used - HTML - CSS - JavaScript - Browser-based interactive simulation The application runs directly in a modern web browser without requiring installation, an account, or a database. 6. Educational Impact The project introduces lunar habitat challenges through interactive learning. It encourages students to understand resource dependencies, engineering trade-offs, sustainability, and decision-making in extreme environments. 7. Limitations The simulation uses simplified educational values and illustrative resource calculations. It is a learning prototype and not a flight-qualified engineering or life-support system. 8. Future Improvements Future versions could incorporate real NASA datasets, more detailed lunar environmental models, additional mission scenarios, and expanded habitat management systems.
